written: 2026-10-27, before Y7(1389) existed and before any radius-24 probe or certificate of 539311 existed. Known at this time: Y3..Y6 of the four frontier rules, interim (unfinished) level-7 Ritz values of 1387 and 539311, the probes of phase12_extrapolation.json (1387 R = 16..24, 539311 R = 16..22, 1389 and 539291 R = 16..22).
goal: exclude 1389 from the maximiser candidates by a certified lower bound E_*(539311) > U(1389), U(1389) the smallest stored exact upper bound on E_*(1389)
why 539311: its sampled probes are the highest of the four at every radius (R = 22: 9.18506 against 9.16748 for 1387), so it reaches a given level at the smallest radius; at R = 24 the 1387 probe (9.19959) is already below Y6(1389) = 9.21050
mu: the smallest multiple of 2^-20 that is >= U + 8 * 2^-20, U = min(Y6(1389), Y7(1389)) as stored (exact rationals) when the certificate starts; the certified value is mu minus Higham's rounding term (1.2e-6 at R = 20), so the 8 units leave room for it
step 1, go/no-go: the 60-ball radius-24 probe of 539311 by the Phase XI protocol (python -u -I audit/phase12_probes.py x539311:539311:24). The probe is the minimum of Rayleigh quotients over sampled legal balls, an upper bound on the smallest certifiable ball value. If it is <= mu the certificate cannot pass and is not run; the outcome is then 'not run: probe below mu'.
step 2, certificate: python -u -I audit/phase12_independent.py cert x539311 24 5 <nproc> <mu> prereg_539311_R24 --ckpt=<dir>; m = 6 instead of 5 if pass 1 rejects any centre at m = 5 (the driver asserts zero rejections). Every distinct legal radius-24 ball must pass the Higham-bounded banded Cholesky at mu.
success: all balls certified and Lambda_R_certified > U: then E_*(539311) > U >= E_*(1389) [C], 1389 is proven inferior, and the certified frontier is {1387, 539311, 539291}
failure: any ball fails: the run may be stopped at the first failure; the lowest failing values are reported and the frontier stays at four
expected [X]: pass. The frozen lower model of phase12_preregistration_extrapolation.json, fitted on R = 16..22, gives Lambda_24(539311) = 9.2170; it overshot the measured 1387 probe at R = 24 by 0.0013. The margin over mu is expected to be about 0.01, and the smallest ball over all distinct balls lies below the 60-ball probe by an unknown amount.
cost estimate: from the Phase XI radius-20 run (24 571 balls, 7506 s with 4 workers, 1.2 core-s per ball): per-ball cost ~ R^7, ball count ~ R^3.1, so about 43 000 balls at about 4.4 core-s, about 13 h on 4 cores plus about 1.5 h of enumeration
meaning: a certificate about 539311 and 1389 only; it says nothing about the order of 1387 and 539311, whose separation needs R of order 60-90 by either model
